method: Started again from the official programme and complete 2026-entry curriculum, then reopened the business, sustainability and Dutch-law minor pages, careers evidence and teacher profile. Reconsidered the defining comparative legal inquiry before inspecting the finished alternatives. Read underlying legal-course profiles and the new environmental/political course evidence, cross-checked all 42 selected source fields against the workbook, then reviewed the exact finished audience selections. This is the same AI, not an independent person or human review.

academicFinding.external: The defining inquiry is comparative legal analysis across jurisdictions, with substantial public/private law. The complete displayed standard core has 25 components and 180 EC, including a 30-EC approved mobility choice and 12-EC thesis. Zero-credit skills/mentoring remain disclosed. The Dutch Law minor changes the final-year core; it is not silently combined with Commercial Law. The LLB identity is corroborated despite the public curriculum table heading saying BSc.
academicFinding.interests: All 27 rows remain reconciled: 16 generators, 10 support topics and one search-only outcome. The narrowed row 145 is supported by sustainability proceedings and a profile reporting prior public-interest-litigation teaching; neither climate-specific syllabus nor current teaching responsibility is established. The sustainability minor is currently linked from the 2026 curriculum; the old registration deadline is not treated as current. Dutch-taught components are disclosed.
academicFinding.closest: Eight direct legal courses (60 EC) provide major legal traditions, interpretation, case briefs, rights, liability, comparative constitutional/private law, international/EU law, arbitration and legal argument. This is material subject/method overlap with Global Law, beyond political/social context. Actual specialist doctrine and a required legal thesis remain gaps; neither exact disciplinary equivalence nor a law-course quota is the standard.
academicFinding.commercial: Seven direct legal courses (52.5 EC) include comparative private, public international, EU and transnational transaction law. Real accounting, finance, economics, firm governance, negotiation and research supply sustained commercial substance linked to the official business minor. It does not promise tax-law training or national professional eligibility.
academicFinding.environmental: Seven direct legal courses (52.5 EC) retain genuine legal analysis. International law includes environmental protection, EU law applies to the green transition, and Living with Water connects law/justice with adaptation. Climate science, life-cycle assessment, governance, policy memos and ethical/political reasoning implement a sustained environmental-governance question. These are complementary subjects; incidental environmental topics alone do not establish a specialist legal sequence, and no legal capstone or litigation syllabus is assumed.

Three concepts pass sequentially; the legitimate Dutch-law candidate stops at the maximum rather than being rejected merely for language or licensing.
